retained_input_verification.scope: Original absolute input path is informational and is never opened; only a local retained input.f32 or input.f32.gz can be verified.

normalization.scope: Whole-source mono sample statistics; normalize valid frames before padding.

notes: VmRSS, VmHWM and VmSwap are exact /proc/<pid>/status fields in kB.
DRM values retain their exact fdinfo field names and units; duplicate client IDs per device are sampled once.
Field type or unit changes are retained as separate observations; maxima are compared only within the same unit.
DRM client maxima can occur at different times; do not add maxima or combine them with RSS as a total or shared GPU peak.
CPU seconds cover the first through last successful sample, excluding earlier process work.
Process count fields retain exact stat/status names; status context-switch counts describe the main thread. Compare cumulative counters only within the same PID/start identity.
Full rows stream to the optional trace; observer memory retains per-process/client maxima and first/last counters rather than sample history.

trace.timestamp_clock: time.monotonic; sampled after process and optional system reads
trace.scheduling_scope: Per-task schedstat sums. Runtime and runqueue wait use ns; timeslices and read_errors are counts. Compare deltas only with identical task_ids and no read errors.
trace.capture_scope: Capture elapsed covers process/system reads before aggregation and trace output. Previous-sample gaps also include trace write time and the requested interval; they do not identify scheduling delays alone.

system_sampling.scope: Host sysfs/proc/statvfs snapshots. Meminfo preserves kB; vmstat fields are separate cumulative kernel counters, not interchangeable units. PSI totals use microseconds and averages use percent. Scratch free includes reserved blocks; available excludes them. RAPL is cumulative energy with a wrap range, not power. Throttle counters can be duplicated across CPU siblings. Missing/denied fields are omitted and counted as errors, never zero-filled.

ui_minute_relation.scope: Whole UI-minute counts only; this does not identify frame events within the native request span.

balanced_comparison.scope: Native replay driver intervals exclude worker source read/OLA/control/ready delivery. Native output is full-window raw output; its hash is not comparable to delivered normalized-restored/OLA hop hashes. The short replay removes controlled UI/audio load and is far shorter than the hour; non-recurrence does not prove cause or a fix.

scope: This is a native-only diagnostic, not the M0 delivered-hop latency gate or an hour audio/UI validation.
Request bounds are exact recorded driver infer-call bounds, including file/native exchange, not GPU batch or graph timestamps.
Host observed timestamps are strictly interior; unsampled edges and capture-start straddles are retained. Reads within a sample are sequential.
Sample medians/flag counts are not time-weighted. Missing/denied readings are never zero-filled.
Counter deltas require complete interior observations and no regressions; process/client identity is retained. DRM engine busy is not useful arithmetic or whole-GPU usage.
RC6/runtime residency and clock samples do not prove why a client waits. PL1 flags are not watts; no causal attribution is made.
Memory/IO PSI and vmstat are system-wide. Zero native major faults alone cannot exclude kernel GEM backing-store activity.
Raw pin paths are metadata; this analyzer never opens runtime/model/source paths. It uses supplied run inputs and optional local input.f32 only.
The short replay changes workload/thermal history and absence of a stall is inconclusive.
